flows.narrative: The freshest verifiable weekly read (to 22 Jul, pre-turmoil) showed a decisive cross-border rotation OUT of developed markets and cash INTO emerging markets — above all China, which drove EM's 2nd-largest weekly haul on record on H2-stimulus optimism, while US equities bled -$7.2bn and Europe -$1.6bn. Cash left money-markets (-$33.9bn) to fund equities (+$30.4bn overall), bonds (+$14.9bn, IG now a long inflow streak), gold (+$2.0bn, largest since April) and crypto (+$0.9bn) — a barbell chasing EM/China upside while hedging Fed-hike and geopolitical risk. Tech drew +$4.0bn (a record ~$52.8bn over four weeks) and Financials +$1.5bn. BofA's Bull & Bear Indicator sits at an extreme 9.6 (sell-signal active since May) and the July FMS shows cash at just 3.6% of AUM (below the 4% contrarian Cash-Rule trigger) — stretched-bullish positioning that amplified both the Wednesday drop and the two-day snapback. The wk-to-29/30-Jul Flow Show could not be cleanly isolated this run; it is the tell on whether the risk-on EM tilt survived the round-trip.

Continued Japan-equity inflows — the persistent DM haven within the rotation (foreigners on track for a record >¥10tn H1 net buy), on governance reform and BoJ normalization. (Korea separately drew a record multi-week haul.)
Europe joined the US on the outflow side as money chased EM/China — a pause in the 2026 pro-international tilt within the DM complex.

Broad bond-fund inflows continued (IG funds on a long weekly inflow streak, govt/Treasury 4 straight) as investors added duration alongside gold — a hedge that pre-dates the post-FOMC yield jump (10Y now ~4.75%, a one-year high); HY OAS ~281bp signals no credit stress yet.

The largest weekly gold-fund inflow since April, on the FOMC-hike/geopolitical hedge bid — validated by spot holding ~$4,054 near a record through the round-trip despite Friday's USD-driven ~1.5% dip. Gold's YTD inflow remains a record; BofA flags elevated net-longs. (Crypto funds +$0.9bn the same week.)
